# Review — iliad-156 (Iliad 24.405–506)

Reviewer: adversarial, two full passes. `t` untouched (checked: every `t`, the header fields and the joined text equal the packet and the pre-review file). All edits to `units.json` made by script. No modern translation consulted. No scansion flags in the packet, so no hand scansion was due. Build and validate not run.

Pass 1: notes (labels, positions, cross-references), Greek to `l` word by word, `l` against `i`, house-table conformity, quotation marks and `mark`/`p`, `l`/`t` line division, `ln`. Pass 2: re-read all 69 units after the edits, then `gloss.json` (every parse against its line, every known form against its use here).

Totals: 1 high, 21 medium (12 in units, 9 in gloss), 14 low (12 in units, 2 in gloss). Nothing unresolved except the table conflict noted at the end.

## Checked and found sound (pass 1 and 2)

Packet-repeated lines: 405, 410, 432 identical to the published `l`/`i`; 441 and 493–494 use the published wording. Paragraph marks (`p`) on 405, 410, 424, 432, 440, 468 match the packet. `ln` of every unit checked against the line it starts in; `l` has the same number of `\n` as `t` in every unit; no `\n` in any `i`. Cross-references in the notes (423, 439, 445/446, 465, 478, 486, 24.255) checked. Case, tense and mood labels checked unit by unit against the Greek, including ἐτύπη with neuter plural ὅσσ’, the dual παρεόντε and τὼ … οἴω, ἰῆς, καθήατο, κίεν, ἆλτο, φάγον, εἴσομαι (from εἶμι), ἀναοίγεσκον and ἵζεσκε.

## Findings considered and refused

- Comma-ended units where the sentence is under four lines (429, 440, 457, 465, 488, 490, 504 and others). The Odyssey rule would join them, but that changes how `t` is cut, which a reviewer may not do; the published Iliad parts (iliad-154, -155) and the pilot also split at commas, so the practice here is established. Not changed.
- 443 `i` "the towers by the ships" against `l` "the towers of the ships". The genitive is loose; the note says "built along the wall". Left.
- 428 ἀπεμνήσαντο "in return": the sense of ἀπο- is not certain, but the note already says "may carry", and `l`/`i` agree. Left.
- 455 τῶν ἄλλων: the note states both readings and the `l` keeps the ambiguity. Left.
- 422 τοι: `l`/`i` render only "your own" (via ἑῆος); the dative of σύ is an ethic particle. Left.
- 430 αὐτόν as "me myself": the other reading (the cup) is not natural with ῥῦσαι. Left.
- 486 `i` "you who are like the gods": a recast of the table's "like the gods", recorded in `new-renderings.md`. Left.
- 463 ἄντην "face to face": the table has two conflicting rows (18.307 "face to face"; 11.590 and 24.223 "right in front"). The drafter followed 18.307, and 24.223 is a verb of looking, so the choice is defensible. Left, but the table should be reconciled at publication.
- 459 and 469 ἐξ ἵππων `i` "from the chariot" against `l` "from the horses": precedent at 11.211. Left.
- 412 `n` "the ship drawn up on the shore with the hut near it": harmless context. Left.

## gloss.json (pass 2)

Present: 82 novel forms plus `__broaden__`; every key of `novel-forms.json` is covered; no ASCII apostrophes; all novel entries under 230 characters; no line numbers. Every parse checked against its line. Wrong or off-sense: none among the novel entries (the odyssey-forms starting point's πεντήκοντά "before the enclitic τοί" is already corrected to μοι). Edits made to gloss.json by script (original saved outside the repository):

| ὄψεσθαι | medium | Known entry pinned to indirect speech after φησί; here the infinitive after ἔλπεται (491). | Broadened. |

| κληῗδα | medium | Known entry "collar-bone"; 455 is a door-bolt. | Broadened. |
| ἄλκιμος | medium | Known entry the adjective; 474 Ἄλκιμος is the man's name. | Broadened. |
| αἰδέομαι | medium | Known entry "+ acc."; 435 takes an infinitive. | Broadened. |

Glosser's `__broaden__` entries for γούνατα, ἐφ, περὶ, ἀπὸ and ὥς checked: each added reading is true of its line (ἐφ’ ὕπνον ἔχευε, περὶ δόρπα πονέοντο, ἀπὸ Τροίηθεν, ὥς περ in 487, λαβὲ/λάβε γούνατα). Known forms checked against their uses and found covered (not listed one by one): πάρα after ἐμεῦ (anastrophe with genitive), σῆμα after περί, γένηται in a fear clause, κακὸν as neuter nominative, τῇ as relative adverb, ἀμφὶ, ἐπί τ’ … ἔλπεται, ἤλυθον 3 pl., ἔτλην, οἷ’, εἴσομαι, θεὸς as predicate.
